doc.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

chapter: Race, audiences and the jazz scene
title: Congressional Black Caucus Jazz Forum and Thelonious Monk Jr.
summary: He spoke on a jazz and family panel with his brother and Branford Marsalis, and met Monk Jr.; their father's 78s inspired them.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Tell me about your visit to the Black Caucus Jazz Forum.

Oh, when was that? That was — it must have been like eight years ago or something. That’s — Congressman John Conyers holds that every year. It’s the Congressional Black Caucus. They meet and discuss jazz related issues. This is where the resolution to declare jazz a national treasure, this is how that was engendered, through these meetings and these discussions. They called me up and said well we’re having a panel about jazz and the family, and we want you to come and speak. And I don’t really come from a jazz family, but maybe they knew about my brother. They didn’t have him on the list, so I called him up and I told them they should call him up. So both of us were there. And one of the Marsalis brothers was there — I think it was Branford, Branford was there. And we were chums from college anyway.

Yeah. And also Thelonious Monk Jr. was there and I started doing some playing with him, in fact I played the bass sax with his — oh it was a tentet I think they had, playing the music of Monk. So we just went around and talked a little bit about how we got involved in jazz and all of that. And of course in most cases it does come through the family somehow. You know our father had old ‘78s. How many times have you heard that story? We listened to dad’s ‘78s and got all excited about the music. There you go. © Hamilton Fillius Archive -9-
He had Firehouse Five, and Louis Armstrong and various things. So that’s what got my brother and I all fired up about Hot music.
